draft.title: Constant rates of change
card: A straight-line graph means the rate of change is constant. Any two points on the line give the same rate.
The rate is the gradient of the line. It is the change in \(y\) for each 1 unit of \(x\). Its unit is the \(y\) unit per \(x\) unit, such as litres per minute.
To find it, pick two points. \(\text{Rate} = \text{rise} \div \text{run}\), with both changes taken in the same order.

Example: a graph of money earned ($) against hours worked passes through (2, 30) and (5, 75). \(\text{Rise} = 75 - 30 = 45\). \(\text{Run} = 5 - 2 = 3\). \(\text{Gradient} = 45 \div 3 = 15\), so the rate is $15 per hour.

4.alt: A line graph of money earned in dollars against hours worked. The line passes through \((2, 30)\) and \((5, 75)\). From \((2, 30)\), a run of 3 across and a rise of 45 up reach \((5, 75)\), so the gradient is \(45 \div 3 = 15\), or $15 per hour.

draft.remember: A straight line means a constant rate of change. The rate is the gradient, in \(y\) units per \(x\) unit.

a.q: A graph of distance against time is a straight line. What does this tell you about the speed?
a.why: A straight line has the same gradient everywhere, so the rate of change is constant. Any two points on the line give the same speed.
a.clue: Think about the gradient of a straight line.

b.q: Priya fills a pool. The graph of litres in the pool against minutes is a straight line through (2, 50) and (6, 130). What is the rate of filling?
b.why: The rate is constant, so use any two points. \(\text{Rise} = 130 - 50 = 80\) litres and \(\text{run} = 6 - 2 = 4\) minutes, so the rate is \(80 \div 4 = 20\) litres per minute. The answer 80 is only the rise.
b.clue: Find the rise and the run first, then divide.
